Senses.Explanation: The standing dare of the Chan hall: whoever claims the matter steps out of the ranks and tries to say it, while the master stakes the seat on the answer. Yunmen Wenyan asks whether anyone has awakened and dares them to come out and say it, answering in their place with the bond of raising a son, Wuzu Fayan raises Deshan's no-questions-tonight ruling and dares any man who disregards his life to come out and say it, promising to meet the old man on the assembly's behalf if none does, Tianyin Yuanxiu sets aside those without proof at Linji's rank-pulling and dares those with proof to come out and say it, verse-breaking the gold-for-six-dusts trade when none appears, and Hanyue Fazang, raising beans and melons on Dengwei, dares any true bare-boned mountain man to come out and say it, then rests on opening fields to store summer water. Fushi Tongxian dares anyone in the crowd who matches the seed-time season to come out and say it, answering himself with white egrets over the misty paddies and orioles in the summer trees, Baiyu Jingsi asks the turning-around phrase outside the night-bright curtain and dares whoever says it in accord to come out — one monk barely steps out and he leaves the seat, Yulin Tongxiu sets his new temple's answers against the old man's urgent-state replies and dares whoever knows the landing place, same or different, to come out and say it, and Zishui dares whoever knows their own wrong to come out and say it, else the Tianhuang will drum his two skins while the crowd lends all ears and he leaves the seat.
